summary: Hoi An is the timber streets after dark. Hue is the Imperial City in the morning. Hanoi is the Old Quarter and the lake.
body: In Hoi An the street is a tight row of tiled timber shophouses, with the covered wooden bridge at the west end and the river the houses back onto. The Japanese bridge is where Nguyễn Thị Minh Khai meets Trần Phú. Tan Ky House is a tube house at 101 Nguyễn Thái Học, shop at the front and the river at the back. The sightseeing fee is check on arrival. From 10 August 2026, Da Nang’s resolution sets 20,000 VND per person per building. The heritage centre’s notices of 26 January 2026 and 16 March 2026 still describe combination tickets of 80,000 VND and 120,000 VND. Ask which rule the desk is using that day.

Hue starts on the south bank of the Perfume River. An adult ticket for the Imperial City is 200,000 VND and does not include the tombs. Hanoi’s old streets are the Old Quarter, Hoan Kiem Lake, and the French-built quarter south of the lake.
